answer: Each identity is a vertex in the EigenTrust trust matrix, where centrality grows only through credible endorsements that are themselves supported by trusted paths. Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed half-life, so an attacker must sustain honest service over time rather than briefly accumulate scores. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits circular praise, while a fresh sybil has near-zero centrality and no reliable bridge to trusted peers; it cannot clear the consensus threshold by spawning identities or leaping the trust ledge.
